clue.text: Bad mistake: error ousting old Labour leader

indicators.note: bad here means messed up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled
ousting says one letter is thrown out of the jumbled pool before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A commentator calls some political blunder a bad mistake that brought down a former Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' and 'ousting' work together: pool MISTAKE and ERROR, throw out O (old), and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named became leader of Britain's Labour Party in 2020 and later Prime Minister.

clue.text: Eels bred in odd places in river

indicators.note: letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on, are the ones taken from the words

explanation.surface: Eels were bred at scattered spots along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A major German river flowing from the Czech Republic to the North Sea at Hamburg.

clue.text: Play concert with introduction deferred

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is put off until the end

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A concert-goer is told the show will start once the introduction has been postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous series of summer concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To play boisterously is to frolic or frisk about, a verb sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Cheers — drank liquid from this!

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: liquid means not fixed in shape, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A toast, then a drinker downs the contents of the vessel in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: you say cheers and drink from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beer mug, often pewter with a handle, from which pub drinkers take their ale.

clue.text: Religious words just audible

indicators.note: audible says the word for just is heard rather than written

parts.note: just as an adjective means fair or right

explanation.surface: A worshipper mumbles prayers that can barely be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just audible' looks like 'barely heard', but 'just' is the word spoken and 'audible' alone signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony or set form of service in worship is spoken liturgy, the words of a ritual.

clue.text: Energy movement generates strong feeling

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
motion is another word for movement

explanation.surface: Physics sounds emotional: energy in motion produces passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirring of the heart such as joy, fear or anger is an intense feeling.

clue.text: Female takes long time in cooking steak

indicators.note: cooking means being worked on or cooked up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman spends ages in the kitchen preparing a steak.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender cut from the narrow end of beef tenderloin, served as a premium steak.

clue.text: Justification for being in Paris?

parts.note: the French phrase translates literally as reason for being, so it is how a Parisian would say justification for existing

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they are in the French capital at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Justification for being in Paris' looks like a reason to visit; the question mark says to read 'in Paris' as 'in French'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression means the purpose that justifies a thing's existence.

clue.text: Distinguished singer keen to make comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the other way, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A celebrated singer is eager to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna, is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Lawless Moab — one country that's evil

indicators.note: lawless means unruly and out of order, so the letters of Moab are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Biblical condemnation: a lawless Moab is a wicked land.
explanation.walkthrough: Moab is an ancient kingdom from the Bible, east of the Dead Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A loathsome or wicked thing, an object of disgust, is an evil as a noun.

clue.text: Latest from all four corners?

definitions.meaning: the latest is fresh information, recent reports
the four compass points north, east, west and south give these initials, as if information arrived from every direction

explanation.surface: Reports said to arrive from every quarter of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The four corners are the compass points, whose initials spell the answer; the question mark flags the folk tale that the word comes from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh information about recent events is the latest, as in 'what's the latest?'

clue.text: Money earned by cabbie? That should turn some heads!

parts.note: screw is old British slang for wages or salary
a cabbie is a taxi driver

explanation.surface: A taxi driver's takings are so impressive they will attract attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn some heads' sounds like attracting admirers, but it means turning the heads of screws.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand tool whose tip fits a slot in a screw's head and turns it.

clue.text: Musical work having name for ship at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A musical piece takes its title from a vessel out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera set aboard a Royal Navy ship is a famous musical work.

clue.text: Host politician, English, in centre

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician acts as host, an Englishman at the centre of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter who introduces acts at a show or on television serves as host.

clue.text: Surrealist in modern studio

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, straddling them

explanation.surface: An avant-garde painter works in a contemporary studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter who was a leading Dada and Surrealist artist.

clue.text: Superhero grabs wheel in transporter

indicators.note: grabs means the superhero's name takes hold of the wheel inside it

parts.note: Batman is the caped DC Comics superhero
a wheel is round, so it is the letter O

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero seizes the steering wheel of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rows or ferries people by water carries them across, so is a transporter.

clue.text: Chauvinist's piece about good love

indicators.note: about means the word for piece goes round the other letters

parts.note: a bit is a piece
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sexist man writes an article about romantic love.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauvinist is someone prejudiced and intolerant of other groups, an extreme partisan.

clue.text: What fills this after downpour's onset?

definitions.text: What fills this after downpour's onset?

indicators.note: after places the water piece behind the first letter
the onset of something is its start, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: rain is what fills a gutter outlet during a storm

explanation.surface: A riddle about what collects in a street outlet once a storm begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the answer itself; the whole clue is the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully or pipe that carries away rainwater fills when a storm starts.

clue.text: Former Italian banker seen in trade fair

parts.note: ex means former
the Po is Italy's longest river, and a river is a banker because it has banks

explanation.surface: A retired Italian financier turns up at a commercial exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A large exhibition where firms show their goods is a trade fair.

clue.text: Giant blunder on pitch disheartened Royle

parts.note: OG is an own goal, a footballer's mistake on the pitch

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle letters, the heart, are removed, leaving the outside

explanation.surface: A huge error on the football field upsets a manager named Royle.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Royle is a former English football player and manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster of folklore, the man-eating creature of fairy tales, is a giant.

clue.text: Adult Glaswegian perhaps in racing venue

parts.note: A is the film rating abbreviation for adult
someone from Glasgow is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: A grown-up from Glasgow at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse is one of Britain's best-known horse racing venues.

clue.text: Normally Laura's out with sweetheart

indicators.note: out means out of place, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Laura usually goes out with her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it is the centre letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or generally, which is what normally says.

clue.text: Pancake containing a lot of fish sauce

indicators.note: containing means the pancake wraps around the fish

parts.note: a taco is a folded tortilla, a kind of flat pancake

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the bass is a fish

explanation.surface: A Mexican pancake filled with lots of fish and a hot sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery red pepper condiment from Louisiana, named after a Mexican state.

clue.text: One able to fill some of the time at work

definitions.text: One able to fill some of the time at work

parts.words: One able to fill some of the time at work
parts.note: the clue reads like a temp covering shifts, but the filling is of teeth, part of a working day spent with cavities

explanation.surface: A stand-in who can cover part of someone's shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill some of the time' suggests filling hours; the person really fills cavities, some of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental professional fills decayed teeth as part of their job.

clue.text: American doctor in excursion to find instrument

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for excursion

parts.note: a tour is an excursion
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An American doctor goes on a trip and comes back with a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum, especially a small one, or the frame used for embroidery: a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Uncertain moment with Juliet disappearing

indicators.note: disappearing means that letter vanishes from the word for moment

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A moment of doubt as Juliet vanishes from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something doubtful or dubious is uncertain.

clue.text: Books in excellent opponent

indicators.note: in puts the books inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 is excellent, written here as AI
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An opponent shown in a fine light in some books.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a person opposed to something, an opponent.

clue.text: Fast food one regularly consumes

definitions.meaning: to fast is to restrict eating, a verb sense of slimming
one's habitual eating, the usual fare

explanation.surface: Fast food that someone eats all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' reads as burgers; split it after 'Fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual food a person eats is their regimen, and going on one means eating less.

clue.text: Troubled king coherent, though losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter goes

parts.note: clear means coherent, easy to follow

explanation.surface: A disturbed monarch who is lucid one moment and loses his head the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic monarch, driven mad by his daughters, is a troubled king.

clue.text: City vehicle carrying European lad around river

indicators.note: carrying means the vehicle holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for lad runs backwards

parts.note: a son is a lad
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A bus carries a European boy around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal wrapping the river, but here it means turned round; the Aire is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Argentina is a large South American city.

clue.text: Some near loathsome British peer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather nasty member of the British nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman ranking above a viscount is a member of the British peerage.

clue.text: Order airborne — dare pilot to break record held

indicators.note: held means the record sits inside the shuffled letters
to break means to smash up, so those letters are reordered

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An order to take off, as someone challenges a pilot to break a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges DARE PILOT into LIDOPTERA, and 'held' puts EP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies and moths form a biological order whose members fly.
